# Kernel command line shared by every boot profile.
# One or more parameters per line; lines starting with '#' are ignored.
# post-image.sh joins the lines and puts the parameters of the verified
# root (dm-mod.create=..., root=/dev/dm-0) in front of them.

# Root filesystem: read-only EROFS, wait for the device to appear.
rootfstype=erofs ro rootwait

# After a kernel panic, reboot instead of hanging. The message stays on
# the screen for ten seconds. A tampered or damaged root partition ends in
# a panic (dm-verity, panic_on_corruption): with this the machine then
# restarts by itself, and from step P0.5d the boot loader falls back to
# the other slot after three failed attempts.
panic=10

# Consoles: the screen first, the serial port last so that it becomes
# /dev/console (systemd messages and the QEMU serial console).
console=tty0 console=ttyS0,115200n8

# Machine identity: the root is read-only and identical on every machine,
# so /etc/machine-id cannot be stored there. systemd derives it from the
# UUID the firmware reports (SMBIOS), which is stable across reboots,
# reinstallations and updates. Without this parameter a new random
# identity would be drawn at every boot, and the journal on the "state"
# partition would start a new directory each time.
systemd.machine_id=firmware

# Keep the boot log readable; raise it when debugging.
loglevel=4
